category-01.name: Executive functions, motivation and task performance

category-09.name: Associated patterns and other reported conditions

symptom-001.name: Task Paralysis
symptom-001.generalDescription: Wanting to do something but feeling unable to make yourself start.

symptom-002.name: Task Initiation Difficulty
symptom-002.generalDescription: Moving from a decision to action takes a disproportionate amount of effort.

symptom-003.name: Procrastination
symptom-003.generalDescription: Putting off tasks even when it is clear that the delay will cause problems.

symptom-004.name: Task Completion Difficulty
symptom-004.generalDescription: Projects reach 80% or 99% completion and simply stay there.

symptom-005.name: Executive Dysfunction
symptom-005.generalDescription: Difficulty planning, prioritizing, organizing and carrying out actions.

symptom-006.name: Task Switching Difficulty
symptom-006.generalDescription: Difficulty stopping one activity and starting another.

symptom-007.name: Side Questing
symptom-007.generalDescription: Starting one thing and finding yourself doing something completely different.

symptom-008.name: Perfectionism
symptom-008.generalDescription: Being unable to move forward because something still does not feel good enough.

symptom-009.name: Overplanning
symptom-009.generalDescription: Spending so much time planning that you never get to doing.

symptom-010.name: Intention–Action Gap
symptom-010.generalDescription: Planning lots of things in the evening for the next day but not actually doing them.

symptom-011.name: Difficulty With Self-Directed Tasks
symptom-011.generalDescription: Finding it easier to act when someone else asks than when you have to take the initiative yourself.

symptom-012.name: Need for Purpose
symptom-012.generalDescription: Finding it hard to follow or remember instructions without understanding the reasoning behind them.

symptom-013.name: Resistance to Prescribed Methods
symptom-013.generalDescription: Being willing to do a task but resisting being told exactly how to do it.

symptom-014.name: Difficulty Prioritizing
symptom-014.generalDescription: Important tasks do not necessarily feel urgent or appealing.

symptom-015.name: Commitment Difficulty
symptom-015.generalDescription: Difficulty committing to decisions, projects or long-term plans.

symptom-016.name: Hyperfocus
symptom-016.generalDescription: Becoming completely absorbed in an interesting activity and losing awareness of your surroundings.

symptom-017.name: Hyperfixation
symptom-017.generalDescription: An intense preoccupation with a particular subject, sometimes briefly before moving on to another.

symptom-018.name: Interest-Based Attention
symptom-018.generalDescription: Being able to concentrate for hours on something interesting but barely at all on something that is not.

symptom-019.name: Chronic Boredom
symptom-019.generalDescription: Feeling that things become boring very quickly.

symptom-020.name: Stimulation Seeking
symptom-020.generalDescription: A need for novelty, interest, excitement or challenge.

symptom-021.name: Understimulation
symptom-021.generalDescription: Significant discomfort when there is not enough interest or activity.

symptom-022.name: Overstimulation
symptom-022.generalDescription: Noise, people or surrounding activity create an overwhelming amount of input.

symptom-023.name: Distractibility
symptom-023.generalDescription: Involuntarily shifting between thoughts and stimuli.

symptom-024.name: Mind Wandering
symptom-024.generalDescription: Your mind drifts away from the current activity to other things.

symptom-025.name: Careless Mistakes
symptom-025.generalDescription: Understanding the task fully but making small mistakes, such as using the wrong sign in a calculation.

symptom-026.name: Interruption Sensitivity
symptom-026.generalDescription: A brief interruption breaks your train of thought and makes it hard to return to it.

symptom-027.name: Mental Restlessness
symptom-027.generalDescription: Feeling that your mind never stops working.

symptom-028.name: Racing Thoughts
symptom-028.generalDescription: A rapid stream of thoughts that is hard to slow down.

symptom-029.name: Constant Internal Music
symptom-029.generalDescription: Songs play in your head repeatedly without a conscious choice.

symptom-030.name: Rumination
symptom-030.generalDescription: Repeatedly returning to past events, mistakes or conversations.

symptom-031.name: Time Blindness
symptom-031.generalDescription: Difficulty sensing how much time has passed or how much time remains.

symptom-032.name: Time Optimism
symptom-032.generalDescription: Overestimating how much you can get done in a given amount of time.

symptom-033.name: Time Overestimation
symptom-033.generalDescription: Assuming a task will take hours and avoiding starting it as a result.

symptom-034.name: Waiting Mode
symptom-034.generalDescription: One appointment in the middle of the day makes it feel impossible to do anything beforehand.

symptom-035.name: Chronic Lateness
symptom-035.generalDescription: Arriving late even when you prepare in advance.

symptom-036.name: Time Anxiety
symptom-036.generalDescription: An intense fear of being late, leading to arriving very early or avoiding plans.

symptom-037.name: Out of Sight, Out of Mind
symptom-037.generalDescription: Things you cannot see effectively stop existing in your day-to-day awareness.

symptom-038.name: Working Memory Difficulties
symptom-038.generalDescription: Difficulty keeping instructions, steps or temporary information in mind.

symptom-039.name: Autobiographical Memory Gaps
symptom-039.generalDescription: Whole periods or events in your life are hard to remember.

symptom-040.name: Forgetting Intentions
symptom-040.generalDescription: Remembering that you meant to do something only after the opportunity has passed.

symptom-041.name: Losing Track of Relationships
symptom-041.generalDescription: Not noticing how long it has been since you last spoke with someone.

symptom-042.name: Habituation to Reminders
symptom-042.generalDescription: An object in plain sight becomes part of the background and you stop noticing it.

symptom-043.name: Emotional Dysregulation
symptom-043.generalDescription: Emotions arise with an intensity that is hard to manage.

symptom-044.name: Rejection Sensitivity / RSD
symptom-044.generalDescription: A strong, distressing emotional response to rejection, criticism or feeling that someone is disappointed in you.

symptom-045.name: Emotional Overwhelm
symptom-045.generalDescription: Relatively small things cause a significant feeling of overwhelm.

symptom-046.name: Emotional Meltdowns
symptom-046.generalDescription: Moments when your ability to cope breaks down.

symptom-047.name: Sudden Anger
symptom-047.generalDescription: Moving very quickly from calm to intense anger.

symptom-048.name: Justice Sensitivity
symptom-048.generalDescription: Difficulty letting go of the feeling that something is unfair.

symptom-049.name: Excessive Empathy
symptom-049.generalDescription: Strongly sharing in other people's emotional distress.

symptom-050.name: Low Self-Esteem
symptom-050.generalDescription: Seeing yourself as lazy, a failure or incapable.

symptom-051.name: Achievement Disconnect
symptom-051.generalDescription: Successes and compliments do not bring a feeling of satisfaction or pride.

symptom-052.name: Chronic Guilt
symptom-052.generalDescription: Feeling guilty about things you have not done, even when you really want to do them.

symptom-053.name: Emotional Exhaustion
symptom-053.generalDescription: Feeling drained by the effort of functioning and coping.

symptom-054.name: Persistent Hypervigilance
symptom-054.generalDescription: A lasting sense of tension or an internal state of emergency.

symptom-055.name: Overexplaining
symptom-055.generalDescription: A need to explain and justify your behavior or decisions in detail.

symptom-056.name: Defensiveness
symptom-056.generalDescription: Experiencing a reminder or request for clarification as personal criticism.

symptom-057.name: Difficulty Maintaining Friendships
symptom-057.generalDescription: Friendships fade because you forget to reach out or catch up.

symptom-058.name: Not Missing People
symptom-058.generalDescription: Not necessarily missing people even when they are important in your life.

symptom-059.name: Social Overwhelm
symptom-059.generalDescription: Being around people can feel exhausting despite wanting connection.

symptom-060.name: Limerence
symptom-060.generalDescription: An intense preoccupation with a particular person and your thoughts and feelings about them.

symptom-061.name: Interrupting Others
symptom-061.generalDescription: Feeling a need to say something immediately before you forget it.

symptom-062.name: Finishing Others' Sentences
symptom-062.generalDescription: Finding it hard to wait for another person to finish speaking.

symptom-063.name: Impulsive Speech
symptom-063.generalDescription: Saying things without thinking enough about how they will be received.

symptom-064.name: Difficulty With Authority
symptom-064.generalDescription: Clashing with managers or authority figures when asking for explanations or questioning instructions.

symptom-065.name: Social Misunderstandings
symptom-065.generalDescription: Innocent questions or behavior are interpreted as defiance, rudeness or disrespect.

symptom-066.name: Romantic Avoidance
symptom-066.generalDescription: Avoiding the possibility of a romantic relationship out of fear of rejection.

symptom-067.name: Impulsivity
symptom-067.generalDescription: Acting before thinking about the consequences.

symptom-068.name: Risk Seeking
symptom-068.generalDescription: A tendency toward gambling, thrills or risky decisions.

symptom-069.name: Substance Use Vulnerability
symptom-069.generalDescription: An increased tendency to develop substance use problems and addiction.

symptom-070.name: Self-Medication
symptom-070.generalDescription: Using cannabis, alcohol or other substances to relax or slow down thoughts.

symptom-071.name: Binge Eating
symptom-071.generalDescription: Eating large amounts, sometimes to cope with boredom or emotions.

symptom-072.name: Food Fixation
symptom-072.generalDescription: Eating the same food for days or weeks and then switching to something else.

symptom-074.name: Persistent Food Noise
symptom-074.generalDescription: An ongoing mental preoccupation with eating.

symptom-075.name: Hypersexuality
symptom-075.generalDescription: Intense sexual desire or preoccupation with sex that sometimes leads to risky behavior.

symptom-076.name: Delayed Sleep Phase
symptom-076.generalDescription: A natural tendency to fall asleep and wake up late.

symptom-077.name: Revenge Bedtime Procrastination
symptom-077.generalDescription: Staying awake to gain personal time, even when tired.

symptom-078.name: Difficulty Falling Asleep
symptom-078.generalDescription: Thoughts do not settle down as bedtime approaches.

symptom-079.name: Sleep Dysregulation
symptom-079.generalDescription: Difficulty maintaining regular sleep times or sleeping through the night.

symptom-080.name: Intrusive Sleep
symptom-080.generalDescription: Sudden sleepiness, especially during activities that are not sufficiently interesting.

symptom-081.name: Chronic Fatigue
symptom-081.generalDescription: Persistent exhaustion, even without significant physical effort.

symptom-082.name: Mental Fatigue
symptom-082.generalDescription: The effort of sustaining attention leaves you feeling drained.

symptom-083.name: Energy Crashes
symptom-083.generalDescription: Shifting from high energy to exhaustion later in the day.

symptom-084.name: Paradoxical Stimulant Response
symptom-084.generalDescription: Reports of calmness or sleepiness after caffeine or stimulant medication. This response is not unique to ADHD and is not diagnostic of it.

symptom-085.name: Sensory Sensitivity
symptom-085.generalDescription: High sensitivity to noise, touch or other sensory input.

symptom-086.name: Auditory Processing Difficulties
symptom-086.generalDescription: Hearing the words but taking time to understand their meaning.

symptom-087.name: Clumsiness
symptom-087.generalDescription: Bumping into objects, dropping things and not noticing your surroundings.

symptom-088.name: Hypermobility
symptom-088.generalDescription: A greater-than-usual range of joint movement, mentioned as a possible associated condition.

symptom-089.name: Dysgraphia
symptom-089.generalDescription: Difficulty with handwriting, including writing that is hard to read.

symptom-090.name: Face Recognition Difficulties
symptom-090.generalDescription: Difficulty recognizing people by their faces.

symptom-091.name: Physical Restlessness
symptom-091.generalDescription: Difficulty standing still or remaining without movement.

symptom-092.name: Fidgeting
symptom-092.generalDescription: Moving your hands, feet or objects while sitting.

symptom-093.name: Ignoring Bodily Signals
symptom-093.generalDescription: Putting off going to the bathroom or ignoring physical needs while engaged in an activity.

symptom-094.name: Difficulty Stopping an Activity
symptom-094.generalDescription: Continuing an interesting activity despite tiredness, pain or needing a break.

symptom-095.name: Doom Piles
symptom-095.generalDescription: Things pile up because they have no regular place or you never finish dealing with them.

symptom-096.name: Organizational Overcompensation
symptom-096.generalDescription: Relying heavily on lists, reminders and routines to avoid forgetting things.

symptom-097.name: Math Difficulties
symptom-097.generalDescription: Difficulty with calculations or understanding mathematical material. This is not a symptom unique to ADHD.

symptom-099.name: Perimenopause-Related Symptom Worsening
symptom-099.generalDescription: Hormonal changes that may worsen attention and regulation difficulties in some women.

symptom-100.name: Co-occurring Physical Conditions
symptom-100.generalDescription: Mentions of POTS, connective tissue problems and inflammatory conditions; these are not ADHD symptoms in themselves.
